newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW - Few buyers seen as market awaits Fed.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Few buyers seen as market awaits Fed.

text.p: The initial public offering market goes into the Easter holiday week with few buyers as it joins other financial markets in nervously awaiting a possible interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
"Right now, they're just no buyers," in the IPO market, said Lizabeth Moses, syndicate manager at Unterberg Harris. "Everyone's sitting back and waiting".
She said they were waiting to see what the Fed will do, and then to see how corporate earnings fare.

Some analysts said that a 25 basis point rise in short-term interest rates by the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee, which meets Tuesday, had already been discounted by the market, and that investors were now fretting about whether it could be a 50 basis point rise.

"My ideal scenario would be that the Fed hikes the rate 25 basis points Tuesday, and then they make some soothing statements about not seeing any need at the moment ... about doing anything else," said William Schreier, managing director of equity capital markets at Salomon Brothers.
The next hurdle to be crossed is the earnings season. Corporate earnings that meet expectations would calm fears and put the stock market on a more even keel, analysts said.
But until then, investors' reluctance to put money into untried companies was leading to the kind of dispirited performance seen last week in the IPO market.
According to Securities Data Co., a paltry $236 million was raised -- not counting Cell Therapeutics' $30 million deal -- making it the slowest week since the week of Jan. 24.
Some IPO deals got pushed back by underwriters balking at the unfriendly environment.

Others came to market by lowering their price. PalEx Inc., FieldWorks Inc., Endocardial Solutions Inc., and Cell Therapeutics all priced below their pricing range, while Omniquip International and Physicians' Specialty priced the shares at the bottom of the expected range.
All in all, according to Securities Data Co., of 127 IPOs priced this year, 43 have come in below their range.
But lower valuations could help pull the IPO market out of its slump, said Richard Smith, managing syndicate director at Montgomery Securities.

"Some deals will get pulled, some deals will get done at much lower valuations, and the lower valuations will basically create success and people will start to make some money again buying IPOs, and it will feed on itself. The success will beget further success."
For this week, the most promising deals are Chicago Bridge & Iron Co NV and AHL Services Inc., according to Vincent Slavin of Cantor Fitzgerald.

Engineering and construction company Chicago Bridge, a unit of Praxair Inc., has the largest deal of the week, with 10.5 million shares and a range of $20 and $23 a share. CS First Boston is lead underwriter.
AHL Services, in a deal lead-managed by Alex Brown, is offering 2.5 million shares expected to price between $11 and $13 each. The company provides contract staffing and management.

John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, said he was seeing a premium expectation of one to 1-1/2 points for Hamilton Bancorp Inc, a Miami, Fla.-based company that focuses on global trade finance.
Other deals that could garner premiums are Auto-By-Tel Corp and Asia Pacific Wire & Cable.
